Areas (owning teams): network, storage, node, scheduling, auth, cli, api-machinery, apps. Choose the single best area.

Label kind as bug only with reproduction steps, version regression, or logs showing controller misbehavior; label as support when report is a question, setup error, 'no effect' / 'can't' / 'failed' without proof of code defect.
If title starts with is/whether/why/how, ends with '?', or requests auth/setup guidance, label kind as support, never bug or feature.
Reports mentioning DRA, DeviceAllocation, DeviceTaintRule, device plugins, or device selectors belong to area node, not scheduling.
Kinds: bug, support, feature. Choose the single best kind.
Areas (owning teams): network, storage, node, scheduling, auth, cli, api-machinery, apps. Choose the single best area.

Choose bug only when report shows concrete wrong value/error with reproducer, logs, or default-config failure; choose support for config questions, CronJob timing, scheduler config, mount propagation, NodePort connectivity, log-size limits, publishNotReadyAddresses-enabled traffic, or version-specific usage without proof of code defect; unsupported standard auth algorithm with config is bug; documentation missing-caveat is bug.

DRA device setup belongs to node, DRA SharedCounters rebuilding/counting and OOM endless pod spawning belong to scheduling/api-machinery not node/apps; CSI CSINode/driver entries and PersistentVolume binding/capacity Quantity overflow belong to storage; StatefulSet dependent GC belongs to apps.

Issues about RBAC enforcement, service-account tokens, certificate authentication, or secrets disclosure belong to auth even when CSI/DRA/storage mentioned; kubectl secret creation, role resource-name validation, scheduler restarts, CoreDNS timeouts, and emptyDir eviction belong to cli, api-machinery, scheduling, apps, storage respectively.

Treat incorrect controller logic, missing retry, duplicate objects, or wrong computed values with evidence as bug; choose feature only for explicit requests for new APIs, fields, or new validation without claim of current wrong output.

Questions phrased as why/whether/how-to/authenticating/is-X-supported or reporting kubectl output or cloud-provider signer behavior are support, not bug; if phrased as should-we-check proposing new validation without wrong output, choose feature.

Kubeconfig usage belongs to auth, but admission-webhook deadlock/upgrade belongs to api-machinery; kubectl describe formatting belongs to cli not node; High I/O NotReady belongs to storage; other Pod eviction/status, PodRequests/Limits, cadvisor belong to node.

Client-go Clientset/Interface usage belongs to api-machinery even when kubectl exec mentioned; enableServiceLinks belongs to network not apps; pod runtimeClassName empty/invalid belongs to node not apps.

Reports about deployment deletion cascading, secrets encryption, OIDC settings, or runAsUser without logs/reproducer are support; UnmountVolume with serviceAccountToken is storage and ingress-nginx CVE is network not auth.

kubectl apply/create/update issues including name handling and deployment updates belong to cli and are support without reproducer, manifests, or logs proving defect; PSP/RBAC bypass claims are support without RBAC YAML and logs.
kubectl top belongs to cli not node; kubectl drain mentioning node/service accounts belongs to auth/node not cli; apiserver high-volume/flood requests from kubelet belong to api-machinery not auth.

Generic Deployment replica placement on master/control-plane nodes and pod phase/status values like OutOfcpu belong to apps (node if taint/kubelet), not scheduling; reserve scheduling for scheduler plugins, preemption, topology, and extender logic.

Selector matchExpressions claims, custom-subnet podCIDR allocation, and run-as-non-root how-to without manifests/logs/reproducer are support not bug/feature; KEP-prefixed proposals for API behavior are feature not bug.

Projected serviceAccountToken file ownership or mount issues belong to storage not auth; pod-spec duplicate ports/protocol merging belongs to network not apps; post-fault or overload unschedulable pods involving volumes belong to storage not scheduling.
Kinds: bug, support, feature. Choose the single best kind.

Label bug only for concrete broken behavior with repro steps or named code fault; OOM/CrashLoop endless spawns, storage-class creation ordering requests, Failed/Cannot logs alone, version-skew errors, and kubectl limits without repro are support, while pods stuck due to named volume/teardown failure is bug.

Deployments, Jobs, CronJobs including schedule/timing, cron-expression help, and workload example questions belong to apps, except kubectl command behavior belongs to cli unless the command is kubectl auth / RBAC / approve verb which belongs to auth, and namespace freeze/block belongs to api-machinery; nodeSelector/node-labels, Priority/Preemption, and Readiness Gates belong to scheduling, not apps.

DRA kubelet, device-plugin, and image pull/re-pull questions belong to node; DRA scheduler failures including failed-to-schedule, scheduler panic, AllocationMode scheduling, ResourceClaim/ResourceSlice scheduling, and Workload API operations belong to scheduling.

Kubeconfig, authentication setup, client-certificate validation, and admission/webhook conversion failures belong to auth, not network/scheduling; node-account drain/RBAC failures belong to auth/node not cli; kubelet-generated apiserver request volume belongs to api-machinery not auth.

Choose area by underlying object, not incidental keyword: client-go/clientset/informer library questions belong to api-machinery even if kubectl is mentioned, and runtimeClassName/runtime validation belongs to node even if apiserver is mentioned.

Core apiserver objects and lifecycle — Secrets (except ServiceAccount token/secret creation/population), EgressSelectorConfiguration, and apiserver upgrade/deadlock issues — belong to api-machinery, not auth or network, even when TLS, webhook, or authentication keywords appear; ServiceAccount token/secret issues belong to auth.

kubectl exec process lifecycle including background-job waiting and orphan/adopted processes belongs to cli, and pod creation failures involving volumes, empty volumes, or concurrent map writes belong to storage, not node even when kubelet, containerd, or pid 1 is mentioned.

Projected/serviceAccountToken volume file ownership belongs to storage not auth; pod ports/protocol merging belongs to network not apps; registry Service/ClusterIP pull failures belong to network/apps not node; node authorizer belongs to auth not api-machinery/node.

Kind is support when body lacks numbered steps/Steps to Reproduce/YAML/manifest/kubectl sequence and lacks fenced multi-line logs; title phrases, single lines, and API/flag/field names alone never count as repro/logs, and support takes precedence over R6/R7.

Determine area by functional domain: stuck Terminating pods and kubelet belong to node not apps, Probe/liveness/readiness belong to apps not cli, KEP Workload API belongs to scheduling even when kubectl mentioned; volumes/volumeMounts/CSINode stay storage, service-account tokens/secrets stay auth.

Concrete blocking/mismatch failures (blocked deletion/eviction, cannot schedule/pull, not refreshed, doesnt match behaviour, tests fail with precondition) count as bug without fenced logs taking precedence over R4; vague 'may have delay', 'inconsistent behaviour', or 'failed: reason withheld' stay support.

Explicit feature-request signals in title/body ('Feature request:', 'Proposal', 'please add/support/allow', 'request to add/allow') make kind feature and take precedence over R4 support and R9 bug even without repro/logs; correcting HTTP status/error type for existing validation stays bug.

Reports with CVE-ID in title or describing security vulnerability/injection (e.g., CVE-*, configuration injection) are kind bug even without reproduction steps or logs, taking precedence over R4 support.

R9 requires a code-level identifier (CamelCase flag, snake_case, file path, or FuncName()) plus concrete wrong behavior including mis-gated conditionals; generic resource words alone (pod/deployment/PVC/storage-class/OOM) never satisfy R9 and stay support per R4.
